newsitem.title: GERMANY: Morgan Stanley lowers German inflation outlook.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley lowers German inflation outlook.

text.p: Investment bank Morgan Stanley said on Monday it was lowering its forecast for German inflation and did not expect the Bundesbank to take action on key interest rates until well into 1998.

Morgan Stanley economist Joachim Fels said in the report that the bank now expected inflation to end the year at the lower end of the Bundesbank's target range of 1.5 to two percent rather than rising above two percent.
"With no obvious inflation trigger at hand, the Bundesbank is likely to leave official interest rates alone until well into 1998," Fels wrote in the report.

The German central bank last changed its major interest rates in April 1996 when it lowered the discount rate, the floor on rates, to 2.50 percent and the Lombard rate, the ceiling on rates, to 4.50 percent.

The bank said it expected German bond yields to rise but less sharply than previously thought. The target for 10-year bund yields by the end of 1997 was now 6.5 percent compared with 6.8 percent in its previous forecast.
The inflation forecast was based on expectations that inflation would remain in the 1.5 percent to 1.8 percent range established in the first few months of 1997.
But preliminary April consumer price data for western Germany released last week showed a drop of 0.1 percent month-on-month for a year-on-year rate of 1.4 percent and down from 1.6 percent in March.
